text:
Asha: Heads-up — seeing repeated 99th pct latency spikes on /v1/generate in us-west-2 since ~10:12 UTC, looks correlated with GPU throttling logs. trace IDs below, can someone start a quick hunt? :eyes:

Kevin: paste the trace ids, please. also which cluster/az?

Asha: usw2-prod-gpupool (k8s). examples: trace.id=4c9a8f2d and 4c9a8f2e; span.ids: span=7a2b3c1 and span=7a2b3c2. low-level logs show "GPU throttled" messages around same timestamps.

Jon: ok running Loki query now — try this to pull the span-linked logs:
```
{app="serving"} |= "span=7a2b3c1" or |= "trace=4c9a8f2d"
| json
| line_format "{timestamp} {pod} {msg}"
```
Will also join the node metrics.

Kevin: also check Prom for GPU thermal/clock limits: grafana panel query: `avg_over_time(nvidia_gpu_throttle_global{job="node-exporter"}[5m])` and `nvidia_gpu_utilization` for that node.

Asha: Loki snippet returned a bunch of "throttled: power cap reached" from pod model-convert-9bf. That job is in the same node as several serving pods.

Jon: that explains it — model-convert batch jobs were backfilled on the GPU pool by the cron yesterday. Can you get k8s events?

Asha: k get events -n infra | grep model-convert -> shows preemption attempts and no evictions due to missing PodDisruptionBudget.

Kevin: quick mitigation: cordon the affected node and drain non-critical batch pods.

Asha: running:
```
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-33-45.usw2-prod
kubectl drain ip-10-0-33-45.usw2-prod --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --selector='app!=serving' --force
```

deploy-bot: [deploy] model-convert cron suspended for 1h by @Asha (reason: transient GPU contention) :thumbsup:

Jon: after drain, p99 dropped back to normal within two minutes. still seeing a single noisy node; adding taint to prevent batch scheduling: `kubectl label node ip-10-0-33-45 batch-no-schedule=true` and update scheduler rules.

Asha: filed an ops ticket with schedule change and partitioning recommendation: move model-convert to a dedicated nodepool or add node-affinity for low-priority instances. ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-1429

Kevin: follow-up action — tune Loki alert for "GPU throttled" rate > 5/min and add a Grafana panel to correlate throttle spikes with per-node power_cap and serving latency. I'll own the alert.

sre-oncall: marking as resolved for incident page. Root cause: unscheduled batch conversion landed on serving GPU nodes, caused power cap throttling => increased token latency. Mitigation: cordon/drain + schedule change + 1h cron pause. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
